$doc: Chip's appearance, as data — the source of the `@component chip` block in css/components.css. Same contract as components/button/definition.json: a plain string is a structural literal, {"token": "x"} binds --x, and an array is a sequence of both. Chip is the case that made `parts` necessary: `.chips` is not a modifier of `.chip`, it is the flex wrapper a group of them sits in, so it cannot be a variant without the word losing its meaning. Everything here was transcribed from the authored block; that a chip is display-only and never interactive is in spec.md, because it is a rule about markup rather than a fact about appearance.

variants.name: solid
variants.$doc: The ONE emphasised fact in a set. It repaints the border as well as the fill — a solid chip keeping the default border would read as a chip with an outline round its ink.

parts.name: group
parts.$doc: The wrapper a set of chips sits in. It provides wrap and gap and nothing else — no chip knows how many siblings it has, which is what keeps the same chip usable in a work-row's tag list and on a project page.
